# hy-memory4dsh
中文 | English
> Three layers of long-term memory for DSH: session, project, personal.
## The problem
DSH has no long-term memory. `AGENTS.md` is a static set of rules you maintain by hand, and session
history only lives inside one session. Start a new conversation and every convention, preference and
past mistake has to be explained again. hy-memory4dsh records them automatically, recalls the relev
ant ones before a turn, and consolidates them after it, across sessions and across projects.
## How it works
The plugin runs inside DSH; the memory engine is Hy-Memory 2.0's Python SDK, hosted in a sidecar pro
cess with its own venv, so there is no service for you to start.
- **Recall** on `agent/pre-step`: search the personal tier, the current project and the current sess
ion, then inject the hits as one sourced user message labelled as background data that may be stale

and is never an instruction.
- **Capture**: batch a window of turns with their tool calls and hand t

he batch to the sidecar, which routes it to the chat, working or coding store.
- **Promotion**: sess
ion memories consolidate into project conventions, and those into personal preferences, giving a ses

sion to project to personal chain.
- **Storage** under `$DSH_HOME/integrations/hy-memory/`; model ca
lls reuse the route you already configured in DSH, and embeddings are local ONNX by default with an
optional remote endpoint.
## Features
- Three tiers: personal, project, session-within-a-project. Browse, search, paginate, edit and delet

e them in the panel.
- Three scenes: chat by default; working and coding use separate productivity s

tores keyed by workspace id.
- Automatic recall and capture, including tool-call traces.
- Settings
> Memory panel: a personal tab and a project/session tab, project picker, independent pagination, ma

ster switch, memory-footprint estimate.
- MemHub coexistence: detection, export, pull (refused with

the holder's pid while MemHub runs) and de-duplicated import.
- Cross-project search on demand; ever

yday recall never mixes other projects in.
- Manual memories: `memory_add` infers the personal or pr

oject tier from the content and reports where it landed.
- Update check and a GitHub link in the pan

from the content and reports where it landed.
- Update check and a GitHub link in the panel footer.

## Compatibility and limits
- A `[search-coding] fact layer empty under scope workspace…` line in the sidecar log means the codi

ng fact
layer is empty for that workspace and the query fell back to experiences (results still retu

rn). It is
SDK observability, not a failed write; silencing all warnings would also hide real failur
bservability, not a failed write; silencing all warnings would also hide real failures, so it stays.
- Project memories belong to a project; session memories follow the project they were created in, so

switching projects hides them.
- Productivity stores are only visible to a search that carries a wo

rkspace id, so capture writes to the chat store unless `capture.productivity` is on.
- During a mode
l outage, reconcile fails; writes retry with backoff, and a final failure keeps the raw text in the

lite layer with an activity entry.
- The bundled embedder is English-first; Chinese recall leans on
a token-overlap fallback. A remote multilingual embedder removes that fallback.
## Privacy
Capture filters credentials before anything leaves the process: API keys, GitHub tokens, AWS keys, S

lack
tokens, bearer headers, private-key blocks and `password=` patterns cause the whole message to

be
dropped from the batch (`looksSensitive`). `permissions.disabledCaptureProjects` lists project ke

ys whose turn capture is skipped entirely: the
"don't remember this project" switch, for a client re

po or private code where memory elsewhere keeps
working. `POST /api/hy-memory/purge {confirm:'PURGE'

}` writes every memory to a
JSONL archive under the integration directory first, then deletes them;

a wrong or missing confirmation
is refused.
## Why was this recalled
Every injection appends one entry to `state.json` under `recallLog` (last 50), holding the turn's qu

ery,
the source (semantic, lexical or both) and, per item, tier, score and rank. `POST /api/hy-memor

y/explain
{id}` returns the newest entry that contains a memory id, so the panel can answer "why is

this row here"
instead of showing an opaque list. The log is capped and stores ids and scores, not m

re"
instead of showing an opaque list. The log is capped and stores ids and scores, not memory text.
